newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium makes lifting bank secrecy easier.
newsitem.headline: Belgium makes lifting bank secrecy easier.

text.p: The Belgian government on Friday said it planned to ease legal requirements to lift the bank secrecy to combat fiscal fraud.

Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt told reporters at the weekly cabinet meeting that fiscal authorities now still had to prove that both the bank and its client were involved in fiscal fraud before being able to launch an investigation.

"In many cases it proved to be virtually impossible to start enquiries at banks because the administration had no way of proving the bank was involved," he said. "We now scrap this requirement (to prove the bank's complicity)."
The government also proposed measures to force Belgians to state in their annual tax returns whether or not they have foreign bank accounts.

"This new obligation will be handled like all false or incomplete tax declarations and will be subject to administrative and penal sanctions if these (foreign accounts) are not declared," Maystadt said.
